title: Re: AI coding agents generate more code, but not more ...
text:
As is standard for academic papers, this is an attempt to describe the state of the world as of when they did the research. But then it takes time to write it up and get it out, after which newspapers report it as current events.

In this case, we're looking at a picture from 2025. The models involved in the main agent results were primarily Claude 3.5 through Sonnet 4.5, GPT-4.1 through GPT-5, and Gemini 2.5. And the paper's design means you're mostly looking at the very initial effects of deployment, before companies developed good review processes.

title: Show HN: Authrot – extract your story elements out of chapters and graph them
text:
I've been working on this app for a couple months, because I needed help outlining my story being written on Google Docs.

I kept adding new characters, and it was difficult for me to keep track of everything going on in the story. I wasn't organized at all.

I do have a subscription to Claude, and it helps, sure, but it didn't exactly build a graph of all the story elements connecting together. Throwing 20 chapters into one context was just terrible at narrowing its focus.

I started building this tool as a way to help me with a few things...

First, was replace Google Docs, because that thing lagged like crazy after 20~ chapters.

Second, was scanning my chapters. I wanted to automate creating a graph of characters, places, factions, objects, monsters, everything. I even started mapping out plots, threads, promises, and events. I threw it all into a database, and am able to lay it all out on the table, in an easy to absorb format.

Want to see where someone traveled throughout the story? What about when they encountered others? Well, now I can! Replacing names and all their aliases throughout the whole book? Easy peasy. What about fixing plot holes? No problem, we can fix those too.

Anyways, I took the extra effort to make it available for everyone by throwing it on on k3s and building the extra framework around the workspace.

It's completely free to use. Scanning chapters requires AI credits, which you get 50 for free at signup. Enough to scan about 15 chapters, or start a new story.

If you need more credits, let me know and I'll gift you more.

title: Re: GLM-Legal...
text:
I’m not sure if this is the right solution, but we clearly need better tools for the legal space. Anthropic's recent policy update makes this abundantly clear:

“When our products are used in ways that can affect someone's health, legal rights, finances, livelihood, or access to essential services, we require there to be a qualified ‘human in the loop’ (that is, someone who has the authority to review and, if necessary, change Claude’s recommendations), and for the individual affected to be told that AI was used.”

Something as common as a family law case has the potential to affect all of the above. Now imagine being a petitioner, respondent, paralegal, or other 3rd party using Claude to review a draft document only to find out that Anthropic has sent your entire file to opposing counsel.

It sounds egregious, but Anthropic is clearly stating they will use their own judgment to control what people can do with its product, and that they will treat customer data as if it's theirs to disseminate. So there's a massive opportunity for an unbiased tool willing to fill this void.
